heading: Serve a built app
body: ty start serves a built bundle. It sends the Brotli or gzip copy of a file that ty bundle wrote when the browser accepts it (see Compressed files). Set the host and port with `server.host` and `server.port` in `server/application.json`, or with the CLI options `--host` and `--port`. The host is an IP address, `localhost` or a name under `.localhost`, such as `shop.localhost`, which binds 127.0.0.1 (ADR 0094). An address that is not loopback also needs `--allow-non-loopback`. A server on a loopback address answers only localhost names, IP addresses, the `tac.origin` host and the names in `server.hosts`; any other `Host` gets 403 with `TY1366`. Behind a reverse proxy, list the names that it sends in `server.hosts`, and list the proxy itself in `server.proxies` (IP addresses or CIDR ranges). Only a listed proxy may send `Forwarded`, `X-Forwarded-*` and `X-Real-IP`; from every other peer, `ty` removes them and writes the real client address (ADR 0096). Environment values from the parent application no longer override these settings. YON_PROFILE selects a Yon profile. The .env file holds private secrets. `YON_JAVASCRIPT_RUNTIME`, `YON_PYTHON_RUNTIME` and `YON_RUBY_RUNTIME` select the runtimes (by default `node`, or `bun` when `node` is not on `PATH`, then `python3` and `ruby`), and this choice is still deployment policy. Handler processes see only a small baseline of environment variables and the names that `server.environment` lists (see Environment variables for handlers).
